solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sam and Bettie working? I've no idea

indicators.note: something working is in operation or being worked on, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether Sam and Bettie are at work shrugs that they have no clue.
explanation.definitionFit: "It beats me" is an everyday idiom admitting a puzzle is beyond you, the same as having no idea.

clue.text: Acquire from ancestors home and their ground

parts.note: IN means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: ground is the past participle of grind, so the letters of the word are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone receives a family house and its land from their forebears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as land in the surface, but it is grind's past tense, signalling an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive property or traits passed down by earlier generations of a family.

clue.text: Robert pulled up mature aromatic herb

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulled up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Rob is a short form of the name Robert
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A man called Robert uprooted a full-grown fragrant plant from the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a blue-flowered plant whose cucumber-scented leaves are used as a culinary herb.

clue.text: Large dog walks in regularly with terriers

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the words walks in

parts.note: Terriers is a nickname for members of the Territorial Army, abbreviated TA

explanation.surface: A big dog trots along on its walks accompanied by some smaller terriers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'walks in', AKI; the TA are Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers, nicknamed Terriers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akita is a big, powerful Japanese breed of dog.

clue.text: Visit diocese

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is to visit them, as in ... a doctor

explanation.surface: A bishop's tour of the churches in his district.
explanation.definitionFit: See means to call on someone, and separately a see is the district a bishop governs.

clue.text: Holiday Linda's arranged somewhere in South Pacific

parts.note: Easter is a public holiday

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Linda has booked a holiday trip to a destination in the South Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter Island, famous for its huge stone heads, is a remote Chilean island in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Aristocrat round in farm building

indicators.note: in places the round letter within the farm building

parts.note: a barn is a building on a farm
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A nobleman is making his rounds through a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a nobleman of the lowest rank in the British peerage.

clue.text: 1930s novel clear regarding musical style

parts.note: bright as in a bright, clear day
on means about or regarding, as in a talk on art
rock is a style of popular music

explanation.surface: A critic says a 1930s book is plainly about a kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton rock is also a striped stick of hard candy sold at that English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton Rock is Graham Greene's 1938 crime novel set in the seaside town's gangland.

clue.text: Aussie native left in disarray without accommodation

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a native Australian animal

indicators.note: in puts the left letter within the word for disarray

parts.note: a mess is a state of disarray

explanation.surface: A kangaroo is left in a chaotic state with nowhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L into MESS after its first letter, making MLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomless means having no room, so lacking any lodging or space to live.

clue.text: Tackle encapsulating inspector's courage

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so the tackle wraps around the inspector

parts.note: harness is tackle, the straps and gear for a horse
DI stands for Detective Inspector; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A tackle on a detective inspector shows bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a rugby verb but is the noun for horse gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardiness is toughness or robustness, the boldness to face hardship.

clue.text: How drink might be downed at home by individual

parts.note: in means at home
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A person drinking alone at home knocks back a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing a drink in one means swallowing it all in a single gulp.

clue.text: Palaver to fix Cockney's cavity following damage

indicators.note: following tells us the cavity comes after the damage

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly, as in a rigged election
to mar is to damage
a Cockney drops the H, so hole becomes 'ole

explanation.surface: A fuss about fixing a London dentist's patient's cavity after harm.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class Londoners whose accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a rigmarole and a palaver are a long-winded, tiresome fuss or procedure.

clue.text: Put too much paint on protective clothing?

definitions.meaning: to apply an excess layer of paint
a heavy coat worn over other clothes for protection

explanation.surface: A decorator overdoes the paint on protective workwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is coating too much; the noun is a warm outer garment.

clue.text: Formal agreement to dine during test

indicators.note: during places the eating within the testing

parts.note: to try is to test
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A formal deal is struck to have dinner while a cricket Test match is on.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formally concluded agreement between nations.

clue.text: The old chaps meeting one Middle Eastern person

parts.note: ye is an old form of 'the'
chaps are men
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Some elderly fellows get together with a man from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni is a native or citizen of Yemen, on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Radical former partner Mike wearing lime perhaps

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: Mike wearing the tree means the tree surrounds him like clothing

parts.note: the lime is one example of a tree
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's ex-husband Mike is dressed in lime green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lime' suggests a colour; 'perhaps' marks it as one kind of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical and extreme both describe views far from the mainstream.

clue.text: Health centre welcomes that woman, a climbing expert?

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the spa holds the woman

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A health resort greets a woman who might be a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that not every Sherpa climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are a Himalayan people famed as mountain guides and porters on Everest.

clue.text: Sunshine transformed front of the military prefab

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters of sunshine are rearranged
the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Sunshine has changed the look of a prefabricated army building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges SUNSHINE into NISSENHU; 'front of' takes T from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a half-cylinder corrugated-iron shelter, quickly assembled for troops.

clue.text: Joe, I'm changing image in text message

indicators.note: changing means altering, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Joe announces he is changing a picture in a text.
explanation.definitionFit: An emoji is a small digital pictogram such as a smiley used in messages.

clue.text: Wine and port Jane half finished

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

indicators.note: only half of the name is finished off, so its first two letters are kept

explanation.surface: Jane has drunk half her wine and half her port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half finished' takes JA, the first half of Jane.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish red wine from the La Rioja region.

clue.text: Female inside definitely astray

indicators.note: inside puts the female letter within the phrase for definitely

parts.note: of course means definitely

explanation.surface: A woman is certainly within the bounds of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Off course means away from the right route, just as astray means wandering off the path.

clue.text: Rich Liberal leaves apartment

indicators.note: leaves means goes out of, so the Liberal letter is removed from the apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

explanation.surface: A wealthy Liberal politician moves out of his apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' looks like wealth; here it means rich food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich food is heavy with fat, cream or butter.

clue.text: Subdued Greek character and rock 'n' roll fan

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s youth devoted to rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: A Greek and a rock 'n' roll enthusiast sit quietly together.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted sound or colour is softened or toned down, so subdued.

clue.text: Sound made by cat to rouse seabird

indicators.note: a sound made by a word means its pronunciation is wanted, a homophone of it

parts.note: kitty is a pet name for a cat
to wake is to rouse

explanation.surface: A cat's noise is enough to stir a gull from its sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound made by' tempts a miaow; it signals KITTY spoken to give KITTI.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull named after its call.
